decisions.quote: Experiment 1 was a conceptual replication of the original study, in which participants directly discriminated the onset timing (early vs. late) of a target sound after listening to a sequence of auditory clicks. This experiment successfully replicated the STEARC effect and revealed that the onset timing is mapped categorically. In Experiments 2, 3a and 3b participants were asked to discriminate the timbre of the stimuli instead of directly assessing the onset timing. In these experiments, no STEARC effect was observed.
decisions.reason: The paper tests the occurrence of Ishihara et al.'s (2008) STEARC effect across four experiments using the original direct-task paradigm (Experiment 1) and modified indirect-task versions of the paradigm (Experiments 2, 3a, and 3b). Because the STEARC effect replicated in Experiment 1 but failed to emerge in Experiments 2, 3a, and 3b, aggregating the paper's experiments testing the effect yields a mixed outcome.

parent_objection: First reply aggregates Experiment1success and Experiments2/3nulls into mixed. But abstract explicitly says the original STEARC effect has only been established with direct timing tasks and no studies investigated whether it occurs automatically in the auditory modality. Introduction and Discussion distinguish conceptual replication in Experiment1 from a new automaticity question in indirect tasks. Determine whether E2/3 truly retest a finding the supplied evidence says Ishihara2008original reported,or test a new extension/automaticity claim absent from the original. Do not exclude based only on an extension label or changed task; do not include solely because the same broad STEARC phenomenon is studied. Codebook requires actual original finding and corresponding new result; close/conceptual failures count only when they re-test that original finding. Inspect source scope and authors own verdict to resolve successful versus mixed. Original identity and type remain accepted.

shipped.outcome_quote: This experiment successfully replicated the STEARC effect. In these experiments, no STEARC effect was observed.

blind_target.authors: Ishihara M, Keller PE, Rossetti Y, Prinz W
blind_target.title: Horizontal spatial representations of time: Evidence for the STEARC effect
blind_target.evidence_quote: Experiment 1 was a conceptual replication of the study by Ishihara et al. 1 , which consisted in a direct task where participants judged whether the onset timing of the target occurred early or late compared to a sequence of reference sounds.
blind_target.outcome_quote: Consistently with the original work by Ishihara et al. 1 , we successfully replicated the STEARC effect by employing a direct task in Experiment 1.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Experiment 1 explicitly and successfully replicates the published direct-task STEARC finding. The other experiments newly test automaticity with indirect auditory tasks, which had not been studied previously; their null effects do not contradict the original direct-task finding.
